title: arrival filter bank benchmark log - Isolde
summary: Exploratory scratchpad for a small filter-bank approach to classify ingress arrival patterns and measure impact on p50/p95/p99 under microburst + background steady load. Idea: use parallel lightweight filters (exponential smoothing variants + short-window histograms) to detect short bursts early and switch batching/priority lane behavior experimentally.
experiment_goals: 1) Measure end-to-end tail impact when switching to a 'burst-detected' fast-path (lower batching window, preempt KV cache logic) for 100-500ms bursts. 2) Compare false-positive rate of filter bank vs single-threshold heuristic. 3) Observe cost in tokens/sec (throughput) when fast-path is toggled frequently.
setup: Cluster: 4x T4 per shard (simulated); runtime build: v1.18.3-feature/continuous-batching; tracing: local perf traces + sample traces to jaeger. Traffic generator: custom Go harness (arrival-scheduler v0.3) with event sequences. KV cache primed to 60% hit baseline. Endpoint: text-gen small model (redwood-3b-quant) with typical 64 token output. Metrics collected: latency histogram (client-side), server processing time, batch sizes, queue depth, KV cache hits, CPU/GPU utilization.
workloads: A: Steady baseline 150 qps Poisson arrivals for 900s. B: Microburst injection: every 30s inject a 300ms burst peaking at 1200 qps (sawtooth envelope). C: Mixed: 1:5 ratio of short bursts (200-500ms) and longer surges (3s at 600 qps). Each run 600s, repeat 6 runs per config. Random seed fixed.
run_results:
Run summary (median of six runs) 

Config: baseline (no fast-path)
- p50: 48ms; p95: 120ms; p99: 310ms; avg batch size: 16; throughput: 145 qps

Config: filter-bank fast-path (ES-alpha=0.25 + short-hist window=50ms)
- p50: 46ms; p95: 95ms; p99: 210ms; avg batch size: 9 (during bursts); throughput: 138 qps

Config: single-threshold (queue-depth > 80 -> fast-path)
- p50: 47ms; p95: 105ms; p99: 260ms; avg batch size: 10; throughput: 140 qps

False positive rate (fraction of steady requests routed to fast-path)
- filter-bank: 0.9% 
- single-threshold: 2.8%

Fast-path switch rate (times/s) during mixed workload:
- filter-bank: 0.18 switches/s
- single-threshold: 0.42 switches/s

Notes on throughput/cost: fast-path reduces batching opportunities -> ~4.5% token/sec increase (cost) for filter-bank vs baseline during heavy burst-run, but p99 improved by ~100ms median. Single-threshold had higher cost (2.2% extra qps lost) and worse p99 than filter-bank.
observations:
- The filter-bank (ensemble of short-window detectors) catches microbursts earlier and with fewer false positives. It tends to favor shorter, more frequent switches which keeps p99 down.
- Over-switching (observed in single-threshold) hurts throughput more than the marginal latency gains.
- KV cache churn observed: fast-path route bypasses prefix caching for first 2 tokens (intentional) leading to a transient cache-hit drop from 60%->44% during bursts, recovers in ~700ms. Could mitigate by warm-starting KV on fast-path (warm prefix copy).
- GPU utilization pattern: filter-bank runs show slightly higher variance (more small batches) but same peak utilization. Memory pressure unchanged.
quick_conclusions: Filter-bank fast-path is promising: best p99 improvements with lower false-positive routing cost than single-threshold. Tradeoff: ~4-5% increased token cost in sustained heavy burst patterns; consider gating fast-path to premium tenant or opt-in feature. For mixed bursts, reduce short-hist sensitivity to cut false positives further.
next_steps:
- Implement warm-prefix copy for fast-path to avoid KV miss penalty and re-run (target reduce p99 by ~20-30ms).
- Add synthetic clients with varied token lengths (16, 64, 256) to see interaction with batching reduction.
- Add experiment: hysteresis on fast-path (min on-time 300ms) to limit oscillation and measure throughput impact.
- Create a lightweight metric (burst-score) to expose in console per-route for eventual UX.
- Sync with batch/queueing folks: sketch rollout plan for dedicated capacity where fast-path toggles can be tied to burst SLAs.
